about: A candidate playbook for ab-run (deck@variant) and runner/ab.py --data. Only the playbook object is read; the deck's data stays in its own file.

playbook.notes: Version 4 with answer rules that fire only when this seat is not the one ahead. Every shipped rule is kept, in its order; rules 1 to 10 and 23 are new. Written from the 200 games this seat played in the league of twelve (league-run #3, seed 20261250: 60 wins, 140 losses) after the first attempt (variants/token-triumph-answers.json, written from the league of four that this deck led with 46%) cast Hour of Reckoning four and a half times as often and won nothing: the leader of a table gains nothing from clearing it. So every new cast rule carries 'opp_power > power' (some single opponent has more power on the battlefield than all of our creatures) and a floor on that opponent's power. What the league games show (seen = in hand or played; cast = cast from hand; held = in hand at the seat's last own turn of a loss): Hour of Reckoning seen 35, cast 12 (all Forge's), held 13; Citywide Bust seen 54, cast 17, held 18; Conclave Tribunal seen 38, cast 28, held 7; Nullmage Shepherd seen 56, on the battlefield in 44, ability used 0 times (AI:RemoveDeck:All); Path to Exile 26/25/0, Devouring Light 49/41/8, Aura Mutation 24/17/5, Sylvan Reclamation 40/27/0, Reclamation Sage 56/44/10 are cast by Forge in most games they are drawn and are left to it. HOUR OF RECKONING (rules 1 to 8; destroy all nontoken creatures, so our tokens stay). Before combat, when an opponent has four creatures and at least eight power and more power than our whole board, and the wipe costs us at most three nontoken creatures: the format cannot subtract, so 'creatures minus tokens <= 3' is a ladder, tokens >= k with creatures <= k + 3 for k = 0, 2, ... 14 (three nontoken creatures on an even count of tokens, two on an odd one). First in the file so that the turn's mana is not first spent on creatures it would kill; main1 only, as in the first attempt (Forge taps no creature for convoke before attacks, so it costs seven mana there). From the league: of the 26 games with the card in hand and six or more lands, the rule would have fired in 12 (from own turn 6 to 12), each time against 6 to 11 nontoken creatures of the opponents, ours 0 to 3; in 16/g00056, 16/g00376, 19/g00339, 8/g00048 and 13/g00153 the seat lost holding it behind on board (Limit Break at nine nontoken creatures, Elven Council at six, Caesar's board), and of the 11 wins with it in hand, 7 are turns on which we were ahead and the rule stays silent. The bar of eight power drops one firing in the league, against a Hail, Caesar board of tokens only that the wipe would not have touched (opp_creatures counts tokens; no condition sees an opponent's nontoken count). CITYWIDE BUST (rule 9; destroy all creatures with toughness 4 or greater). No condition sees toughness, so the rule keeps our side clean by name: not with any of our base-toughness-4 creatures (Thunderfoot Baloth, Verdant Force, Trostani Discordant, Loyal Guardian, Great Oak Guardian, Nullmage Shepherd), Champion of Lambholt (grows with counters) or the anthems that lift a 1/1 to toughness 4 (Collective Blessing, Dictate of Heliod) on the battlefield; and only when an opponent has more power than we do and at least eight. From the league (toughness from the card scripts plus our own anthems, opponents' anthems not counted, so a floor): on the own turns with Bust in hand, three lands and none of our creatures at toughness 4, the opponents had a toughness-4 creature on 107 of the 110 turns we were behind and two or more on 89; the rule would have fired in 32 of the 50 games with the card and three lands, earlier than Forge's own cast in most, hitting a median of three of the opponents' creatures (Caesar, Galadriel, Omo, Cloud and the Eldrazi among them). Forge's own casts are not held back: this adds casts when behind. CONCLAVE TRIBUNAL (rule 10). Shipped, it is Forge's and goes out after the creatures; when an opponent has six power and more than our board it is now cast first, before the turn's development (its target is still Forge's choice). From the league: the rule fires a turn or more before Forge's cast in about ten of the 28 games with it in hand and four lands. NULLMAGE SHEPHERD (rule 23; AI:RemoveDeck:All, so Forge never activates it: 0 of the league's 44 games it was on the battlefield). After combat, with four untapped creatures that can tap, when our life is above the biggest attack any one opponent has (life > threat), on the artifact or enchantment Forge's logic picks (it will not aim at our own, and the rule does nothing if Forge sees no target worth it). Targets on offer in the pool: Propaganda, Impact Tremors, Marshal's Anthem, Assemble the Legion, Cloud's equipment, Anikthea. LEFT WITH FORGE: Path to Exile, Devouring Light (instant, an attacking or blocking creature), Aura Mutation, Sylvan Reclamation and Reclamation Sage (Forge's targets: Sylvan Reclamation went at Sol Ring and signets as often as at threats, which no rule can change), Rootborn Defenses and Dauntless Escort (answers to a wipe on another player's turn). LOCAL TABLES: see the agent report (docs/agents/reports).
